item: The rollup build compares the library generation it began under at every stage boundary, so a corpus swap between batches or in the aggregate stage stops it instead of producing a rollup no corpus made
summary: The build commits between batches, which returns its connection to the pool, and the generation guard's checkout refusal is answered by a fresh connection on the NEW file, so a swap that landed between two batches or in the DuckDB-only aggregate stage raised nothing: the build went on across both corpora and swapped a mixed rollup in (measured by the Opus read of #1547: select, commit, swap, select on one session returned the new file's row). Now _build_inmemory_and_swap reads library_generation.current() before its session reads a row and the per-batch hook compares it with the guard's own valid() after each batch of mentions, when the aggregate begins and after each shard, when the keywords stage begins and ends, and once more before the rollup is swapped in; a mismatch raises StaleLibraryError, which #1547's branch turns into no hold, library-replaced in last_decline, and a rebuild on the next request. No new fixed number (a boundary, not a timer). The comparison is made under library_generation.connecting() (the shared level), because swap_window moves the generation first and a bare valid() would refuse a build for a swap that is later refused before it touches anything; a build stopped by the memory guard or DuckDB's limit compares before it composes its hold, so no hold carries the new file's count. Tests do a real swap on a guarded engine and run the hook inside the real build_keyword_daily (which shows the refusal comes out of that build unchanged, not that the build reads the swapped file); with the comparison removed 13 of 16 fail (with duckdb installed), and each mutant (no shared level, no skip-path comparison, no hook check) fails its own cases. LIMITS: the persisted refresh (refresh_keyword_daily) has no hook and is not compared; a swap between the last comparison and the swap-in under _LOCK is the window's width (milliseconds: the session commit and close, the progress end and the marker clear run between them); Windows handles and an identical-token restore not measured.
